subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported hard-limit-only or fully-off automatic compaction mode, and should persisted compaction entries carry a closed trigger reason?
rationale: Current main partially fixes Anthropic context-usage overcounting and already respects pruning off, but the remaining request changes compaction safety semantics, config surface, and transcript metadata.

options.title: Define hard-limit semantics
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction where requested, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep current compaction policy
options.body: Treat automatic compaction as always available by design and narrow follow-up work to verified false low-context triggers and clearer docs.

options.title: Require live Anthropic proof first
options.body: Wait for a current-main Anthropic API-key reproduction before accepting new compaction semantics beyond the existing partial fixes.

recommendation.title: Define hard-limit semantics
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction where requested, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses compaction safety, config contract, and docs surfaces where recent adjacent history points to steipete.
